title: A file the project does not have
plain: A file the project does not have
summary: A site-relative `src:`, `poster:`, `captions:` or `transcript:` names a file that is not in `public/`; the page asks for it and gets nothing.
description: A site-relative `src:`, `poster:`, `captions:` or `transcript:` names a file that is not in `public/`; the page asks for it and gets nothing.
why:
Warning. In a project whose `public/` has no `img/hero.png` (the example
is not compiled here: what it draws depends on the project's files):

```wf no-check
page P(path: "/", title: "T", description: "D") {
    Heading("Team").h1
    Image(src: "/img/hero.png", alt: "The team at the launch")
}
```

The same goes for a `Video`'s `poster:` and `captions:`, an `Audio`'s
`transcript:`, and a worker's `spawn("/workers/css.js")`: the page asks
for the file and gets a 404.
fix:
put the file in `public/`, or correct
the path.

title: A persisted value storage cannot keep
plain: A persisted value storage cannot keep
summary: `persist` writes its value to the browser's storage as JSON; a function, a file or a promise does not survive it.
description: `persist` writes its value to the browser's storage as JSON; a function, a file or a promise does not survive it.
printed:
error[D02]: `persist pick` keeps a function, which cannot be written to the browser's storage
 --> src/App.wf:2:5
  |
2 |     persist pick = (x) => x + 1
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Keep what it is made from — a name, an id, the data — and build it again when it is read
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/D02
fix:
Keep what it is made from — a name, an id, the data — and build
the rest when it is read.

title: A persisted value every instance shares
plain: A persisted value every instance shares
summary: A `persist` in a component placed more than once, or in a loop, is one stored value for all of them. `key:` gives each its own.
description: A `persist` in a component placed more than once, or in a loop, is one stored value for all of them. `key:` gives each its own.
printed:
warning[D03]: `persist open` is in `Panel`, which is placed more than once, so every one of them reads and writes one stored value
 --> src/App.wf:2:5
  |
2 |     persist open = false
  |     ^^^^^^^
  = help: Give each its own: `persist open = false { key: id }`, with `id` a prop that tells them apart
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/D03
why: Warning.
fix:
Give each instance its own key: `persist open = false { key: title
}`, with a prop that tells them apart.

title: A persisted shape changed with no new version
plain: A persisted shape changed with no new version
summary: What a returning reader's browser holds is the old shape; the page reads it as the new one. Raising `version:`, with a `migrate` step, brings it forward.
description: What a returning reader's browser holds is the old shape; the page reads it as the new one. Raising `version:`, with a `migrate` step, brings it forward.
why:
Warning. The build remembers what each `persist` held (in
`.wf-cache/persist.json`); when that changes — `persist items: [String] = []`
becomes `persist items: Lists = Lists()` — and `version:` does not, a
returning reader's browser hands the old shape to code written for the new
one.
fix:
raise `version:` and add `migrate 1 -> 2 { … }` to bring the
old value forward.

title: An asset from another origin with no integrity hash
plain: An asset from another origin with no integrity hash
summary: A stylesheet, font or script loaded from another origin is code that origin can change after you read it. A `meta.integrity` hash is how the browser checks it has not.
description: A stylesheet, font or script loaded from another origin is code that origin can change after you read it. A `meta.integrity` hash is how the browser…
why:
Warning. A font, stylesheet or script in `meta.fonts`, `meta.stylesheets`
or `meta.scripts` from another origin, with no hash in `meta.integrity`.
fix:
add its `sha384-…` hash to `meta.integrity` (the CDN usually
publishes it). Google Fonts is exempt: its stylesheet differs per browser.

title: A script loaded on consent, with nothing to ask for it
plain: A script loaded on consent, with nothing to ask for it
summary: A `meta.scripts` entry marked `"load": "consent"` loads only once the reader accepts in a `ConsentBanner`. With no banner in the program, nobody is asked, and it never loads.
description: A `meta.scripts` entry marked `"load": "consent"` loads only once the reader accepts in a `ConsentBanner`. With no banner in the program, nobody is…
why:
Warning. A `meta.scripts` entry is marked `"load": "consent"`, so it loads
only once the reader accepts in a `ConsentBanner` — and the program has no
`ConsentBanner`, so nobody is asked and the script never loads.
fix:
place a `ConsentBanner("…")` in `app`, where every page shows it,
or drop `"load": "consent"` if the script needs no consent.

title: A path that names no parameter
plain: A path that names no parameter
summary: An endpoint's path names its parameters, `at "users/{id}"`: each `{name}` is filled by the parameter of that name, and one that no parameter fills would be sent as written. A parameter has one place — the path, a header or a cookie.
printed:
error[N01]: `Backend.user` is at `users/{id}`, and no parameter fills `{id}`
 --> src/App.wf:4:5
  |
4 |     get user(userId: String) at "users/{id}" -> User!
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Name a parameter `id`; it takes `userId`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/N01
why:
Error.

An endpoint's path names the parameters that go in it: `at "users/{id}"`
is sent as `users/7` when the call passes `id: "7"`. A `{name}` that no
parameter of the endpoint fills would be sent as it is written, braces and
all, and the server would answer a path it does not have.

A parameter also has one place. One the path names goes in the path; it
cannot be sent as a header or a cookie too.
fix:
Name the parameter as the path does, or write the path with the
parameter's name. A parameter meant for a header or a cookie is taken out
of the path.

title: A resource over a write
plain: A resource over a write
summary: A `resource` asks whenever the page draws it and whenever what it reads changes. A write — a `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` — is sent when something happens, from an action, once.
printed:
error[N02]: `resource made` reads `Backend.create`, a `POST`: a write is sent when something happens, not whenever the page draws
 --> src/App.wf:8:5
  |
8 |     resource made = Backend.create(title: "Milk")
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Call it from an action: `action save() { match await Backend.create(…) { .ok(v) { … } .err(e) { … } } }`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/N02
why:
Error.

A `resource` asks whenever the page draws it, and again whenever what it
reads changes or the page comes back into focus. That is right for a read,
which changes nothing on the server. A write — a `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or
`DELETE` — would then be sent again each time: a second todo, a second
order. A write is sent once, when something happens, from an action or a
handler.

`.update(change)`, which shows a change before the server agrees, is a
read's for the same reason: it changes what a resource over the read shows.
fix:
Call the write from a handler or an action, and `match` what it
returns. If the page shows what the write changed, read it with a `get`,
and say on the write that it `invalidates` that read.

title: A `try` with nowhere to pass its error
plain: A try with nowhere to pass its error
summary: `try` gives a result's value, or returns its error from the action it is in, as the action's own. The action must say what it fails with, and that must be able to hold the error: the same type, an `HttpError` into an error enum's `http` case, or another error enum through its `http` case once its other cases are handled.
description: `try` returns a result's error from the action it is in, so the action must say what it fails with, and that must be able to hold the error.
printed:
error[N03]: `try` returns `await Backend.user(…)`'s error from the action, and the action declares nothing it returns
  --> src/App.wf:10:20
   |
10 |         let user = try await Backend.user(id: id)
   |                    ^^^
   = help: Say what it fails with: `-> User!`, or `match` the result here
   = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/N03
why:
Error.

`try r` gives the value of the result `r` when it is `.ok`, and when it is
`.err` it returns the error from the action at once, as the action's own.
So the action says what it fails with — `-> T ! E`, `-> T!`, `-> ! E` or
`-> !` — and that has to be able to hold the error:

- the same error type is passed up as it is;
- an `HttpError` (from a call declared `-> T!`) becomes an error enum's
  `.http(e)`;
- another error enum passes up only through its `http` case: any other
  case of it must be handled first, with `match`, since the action's enum
  has no case to put it in.

In a handler, outside any action, `try` reports a failure where the page
reports errors instead.
fix:
Declare what the action fails with, or `match` the result where
the call is made and handle each case there.

title: A result nothing reads
plain: A result nothing reads
summary: `await Backend.users.create(body: draft)` written on its own drops what came back: whether the user was made, or why not. Match it, or pass a failure up with `try`.
printed:
warning[N04]: what `await Backend.create(…)` answers is not read: whether it worked goes nowhere
 --> src/App.wf:9:9
  |
9 |         await Backend.create(title: title)
  |         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Match it — `match await … { .ok(v) { … } .err(e) { … } }` — or pass a failure up with `try await …`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/N04
why:
Warning.

A call of an endpoint never throws: it returns a result, `.ok(value)` or
`.err(error)`. Awaited on its own, the result is dropped, and with it
whether the call worked. If the server refused the todo, or the network was
gone, nothing on the page says so.
fix:
`match` the result and say what happened in each case, or write
`try await …` in an action that declares an error, to pass a failure up to
whatever called it.

title: An `invalidates` naming what the contract does not have
plain: An invalidates naming what the contract does not have
summary: A write's `invalidates [list, byId(id)]` names the reads a success makes stale, each a `get` of the same group, each argument one of the write's own parameters. A name the group does not have would make nothing stale.
printed:
error[N05]: `Backend.todos.create` invalidates `all`, which `Backend.todos` has no read of
 --> src/App.wf:9:18
  |
9 |     invalidates [all]
  |                  ^^^
  = help: It may name `list`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/N05
why:
Error.

A write's `invalidates [list, byId(id)]` names the reads that a success
makes stale: every resource on the page over one of them asks again. Each
name is a `get` of the same group, and each argument is one of the write's
own parameters, so that `byId(id)` refreshes the item the write changed. A
name the group does not have would make nothing stale, and the page would
keep showing what the write changed.

A read changes nothing, so an `invalidates` on a `get` is refused too.
fix: Name a read the group declares, with arguments the write takes.

title: A form 7.0 removed
plain: A form 7.0 removed
summary: `fetch(…)`, an endpoint that does not say how it fails, `errors { }`, and a read's `loading`/`error`/`ready` arms, `.data`, `.state`, `.refreshing` and `on:` were how 6.x asked a service for things and read the answer. In 7.0 a request is `http.get(…)` or an endpoint declared `-> T ! E` or `-> T!`, whose answer is a result, and a read is one value: `.loading`, `.failed(e)` or `.loaded(value)`. Each form has its fix.
description: `fetch(…)`, an endpoint that does not say how it fails, `errors { }`, and a read's `loading`/`error`/`ready` arms, `.data`, `.state`, `.refreshing` and `on:` were how 6.x asked a service for things and read the answer. In 7.0 a request is `http.get(…)` or an endpoint declared `-> T ! E` or `-> T!`, whose answer is a result, and a read is one value: `.loading`, `.failed(e)` or `.loaded(value)`. Each form has its fix.
printed:
error[N08]: `resource rows = fetch(…)`: `fetch` is the browser's, and a read is `http.get(…)`
 --> src/App.wf:4:5
  |
4 |     resource rows: [Row] = fetch("/api/rows")
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Write `http.get(url, …)` — or `http.post`, `http.put` for another method — with the type it holds: `resource rows: [Row] = http.get(…)`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/N08
why:
Error.

WebFluent 6 asked a service for things, and read the answers, in ways
that 7.0 does not keep:

- **`fetch(…)`**, in a `resource` or an action. A request is now
  `http.get(url, …)`, `http.post(…)`, `http.put(…)`, `http.patch(…)`,
  `http.delete(…)`; in an action its answer is a result — `.ok(value)` or
  `.err(e)` with an `HttpError` — read with `try` or `match`, and its type
  is named where the answer goes: `let rows: [Row] = try await
  http.get(url)`. `window.fetch` is the browser's own, untouched.
- **An endpoint that does not say how it fails**: `get user(id: String) at "user" ->
  User`. Every call of an endpoint answers with a result, so it is declared
  `-> User!` — a `User` or an `HttpError` — or `-> User ! UserError` with an
  error enum; `-> !` for one that answers with nothing.
- **`errors { 422 -> T }`**, which typed a failure's body. A status is now
  a case of an error enum, carrying its body: `unprocessableContent(problem:
  T) on 422`, beside `http(error: HttpError)`.
- **A read's 6.x arms and members.** A `resource` is one value:
  `.loading`, `.failed(e)` or `.loaded(value, refreshing, stale)`. The arms
  `loading`, `error(e)` and `ready(v)` are those cases; `.data` is
  `.value`, `.refreshing` is `.isRefreshing`, and `.state` is asked as
  `.isLoading`, `.isLoaded` or `.isFailed`. `on:` is `refresh:` —
  `.onFocus`, `.onReconnect`, `.every(30.seconds)`, `.never`.
- **A service's `headers { }` and hooks.** What touches a request is
  middleware, in the order written: `headers { Authorization: "Bearer
  {Session.token}" }` is `middleware [bearer(Session.token)]`, any other
  header `header("Accept-Language", Session.language)`; `on error(e)`
  refreshing a token and returning `"retry"` is `refreshOn401(Session.refresh)`,
  written before `bearer`; anything else an `on request`, `on response` or
  `on error` hook did is a `middleware name(req, next) { … }` of the
  project's, named in the list.
- **An endpoint with no `at`, and a path's `:name`.** 6.x made a path from
  the endpoint's name when it gave none; 7.0 asks for it, `get users() at
  "users" -> [User]!`, and names a parameter in it as OpenAPI does, `at
  "users/{id}"`.
- **A group that sets how requests are sent.** `api Backend.users { … }`
  is reached through `Backend` and sends what it sends: its `base:`,
  `timeout:`, `retry:` and `middleware` are written on `Backend`.
fix:
The editor's quick fix and `wf fix --code N08` write `http.get`
for `fetch`, `-> T!` for an endpoint, a read's 7.0 arms, `.value`,
`.isRefreshing`, `refresh:`, a missing `at` and `{name}` for `:name`. An `errors { }` block, a `fetch` with a
`method:` and a read's `.state` are rewritten by hand.

title: A retry asked of a write that is not idempotent
plain: A retry asked of a write that is not idempotent
summary: A `POST` or `PATCH` whose answer was lost may have been taken, and sent again it would be taken twice — a second order. So it is retried, or replayed offline, only when its endpoint is marked `idempotent`, which sends one `Idempotency-Key` on every try; a `retry:` on any other write does nothing.
description: A `POST` or `PATCH` whose answer was lost may have been taken, and sent again it would be taken twice — a second order. So it is retried, or replayed offline, only when its endpoint is marked `idempotent`, which sends one `Idempotency-Key` on every try; a `retry:` on any other write does nothing.
printed:
warning[N09]: `retry:` on `Shop.placeOrder`, a `POST` its contract does not mark `idempotent`: it is not retried
  --> src/App.wf:12:85
   |
12 |             let made = try await Shop.placeOrder(body: Order(id: "o-1", total: 12), retry: 3)
   |                                                                                     ^^^^^^
   = help: If the server takes it once whatever the number of tries, mark it: `post placeOrder(…) -> … idempotent`
   = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/N09
why:
Warning.

A `POST` or `PATCH` whose answer was lost — a timeout, a dropped
connection — may have been taken by the server. Sent again, it would be
taken twice: a second order, a second payment. So a write is retried, or
kept to replay when the network returns, only when its endpoint is marked
`idempotent`, which says the server does it once however many times it is
sent. Such an endpoint sends one `Idempotency-Key` with every try of a call,
for the server to tell the tries apart from a second call. A `retry:` on any
other write does nothing.
fix:
When the server keeps an `Idempotency-Key` — Stripe's API and many
payment services do — mark the endpoint `idempotent`. Otherwise take the
`retry:` off, and let the reader decide to try again.

title: `Any` or `Map` where a service meets the program
plain: Any or Map where a service meets the program
summary: What crosses to a service — a parameter, a body, an answer, what a read holds — has a type the program names: a `type` with its fields, a dictionary, or `Json` for JSON whose shape is open. `Any` and `Map` say nothing of what arrives, so nothing about it can be checked.
description: What crosses to a service has a type the program names: a record, a dictionary, or `Json` — never `Any` or `Map`.
printed:
error[N11]: `body` of `Backend.signUp` is `Map`, which says nothing of what it holds
 --> src/App.wf:2:5
  |
2 |     post signUp(body: Map) at "users" -> !
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Name it: a `type` with its fields, a dictionary `[String: T]`, or `Json` for JSON whose shape is open
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/N11
why:
Error.

A request is where a program meets data it did not make. What crosses —
an endpoint's parameters and body, its answer, what a `resource` holds,
what an `http` call answers — is a type the program names, so the checker
can hold every use of it to its fields and every answer can be checked
when it arrives. `Any` and `Map` say nothing of what is in them.

`http.get` names what it answers where the answer goes: `let rows: [Row] =
try await http.get(url)`, or `resource rows: [Row] = http.get(url)`. A
write whose answer nothing reads needs no type for it.
fix:
Name the type: a `type` with the fields the service sends, a
dictionary `[String: T]` for one keyed by name, or `Json` for JSON whose
shape really is open, which is then matched or decoded. The quick fix
writes `Json`.

title: An error enum that is not shaped as one
plain: An error enum that is not shaped as one
summary: An error enum names the statuses a service answers with, each a case carrying the body of its status, and keeps one `http(error: HttpError)` case for everything else — no network, a timeout, a status it does not name. A case with no status or more than one value, a status named twice, or no `http` case leaves a failure with nowhere to go.
description: An error enum names the statuses a service answers with, each a case with one value, and keeps one `http(error: HttpError)` case for the rest.
printed:
error[N12]: `SaveError` names a status, so it is an error enum, and keeps no `http` case
 --> src/App.wf:3:1
  |
3 | enum SaveError {
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Add `http(error: HttpError)`: what goes wrong that no case names — no network, a timeout, another status — arrives there
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/N12
why:
Error.

An error enum is what an endpoint declared `-> T ! E` fails with. Each
status the service answers with is a case of its own, `on` its status,
carrying the body that status sends; and one case, `http(error:
HttpError)`, takes everything else — no network, a timeout, a status no
case names. An enum that names a status is an error enum, and is held to
that shape:

- exactly one `http(error: HttpError)` case, which names no status;
- every other case names its status and carries one value;
- no status named twice.

An endpoint may also be declared `-> T!`, when the service declares no
statuses of its own: it fails with an `HttpError`.
fix:
Add the `http(error: HttpError)` case, give each other case one
value and its status, and keep each status to one case.

title: A `pages` or `streamed` an endpoint cannot have
plain: A pages or streamed an endpoint cannot have
summary: A read may answer a page at a time — `pages .number(param: page)`, `.cursor(param: after, next: p => p.next)` or `.link` — or a line at a time, `streamed`. Each is a read's, each gathers a list, and each names what it needs: the parameter the next page goes in, which the first call need not give, and where a page's items are when it is not a list itself. `for await` walks only a `streamed` endpoint's lines.
description: An endpoint that pages names the parameter the next page goes in and where a page's items are; one that streams answers a list. Each is a read's.
printed:
error[N14]: `pages .cursor` on `Social.feed` says nothing of where the next page starts
 --> src/App.wf:5:5
  |
5 |     get feed(after: String?) at "feed" -> FeedPage!
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Name it from a page: `next: p => p.nextCursor`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/N14
why:
Error.

An endpoint may answer more than once for one read. It may answer a page
at a time:

- `pages .number(param: page)` asks for page 1, 2, 3 and stops at the
  first empty page;
- `pages .cursor(param: after, next: p => p.nextCursor)` asks for the next
  page with the cursor the last one gave, and stops when there is none;
- `pages .link` asks for the address the answer's `Link` header names
  `rel="next"` (RFC 8288), and stops when there is none.

Or it may answer a line at a time, `-> [Line]! streamed`, one JSON value
a line.

Either way a read of it holds a list: every page's items, or every line
so far. So each must say what it needs. The parameter the next page goes
in is one of the endpoint's, and the first call need not give it: it has
a default, or may be null. A page that is not a list itself says where
its items are, `items: p => p.posts`. A streamed endpoint answers a list.
Both are reads, `get`s: a write is sent once. And `for await` walks only
a streamed endpoint's lines.
fix:
Say what the style needs — the parameter, where the next page
starts, where a page's items are — or answer a list.

title: A message one locale has and another does not
plain: A message one locale has and another does not
summary: A reader in the locale that lacks it sees the default locale's words instead of their own — or, where the default locale is the one that lacks it, the key.
description: A reader in the locale that lacks it sees the default locale's words instead of their own — or, where the default locale is the one that lacks it, the key.
why:
Warning. `nav.blog` in `en.json` and not in `ar.json`: a reader in Arabic
sees the English message, since a key the reader's locale lacks falls back to
the default locale's. Where the default locale is the one that lacks it, the
reader sees the key itself. A locale with no file at all reads every message
from the default locale's.

Under `i18n.literals`, the default locale's words are their own keys, so its
table lacking one is no fault and is not reported.
fix:
translate it, or
remove it from the others.

title: Words a reader sees that are not translated
plain: Words a reader sees that are not translated
summary: Under `i18n.literals`, text that splices more than a name, or a value shown by a name that does not say it is words, is never looked up: every reader sees it as written.
description: Under `i18n.literals`, text that splices more than a name, or a value shown by a name that does not say it is words, is never looked up: every reader…
why:
Warning, under `"literals": true`. `Text("{plural(n, "file")} found")`
splices a call, so no table can key it; `derived said = "{n} errors"`
shown as `Text(said)` is not looked up, because only a value whose name
says it is words (`saidText`, `errorsLabel`) is. A reader in Arabic sees
both in English.
fix:
splice names, `derived filesText = "{n} files"`
then `Text("{filesText} found")`, and name what is words as words.

title: An allow that allows nothing
plain: An allow that allows nothing
summary: A `// wf-allow(CODE)` comment covers the next line of code (or its own, at the end of one); when nothing it names is reported there, or it names an error no allow may silence, it is reported itself — so allows cannot outlive what they were written for.
description: A `// wf-allow(CODE)` comment covers the next line of code (or its own, at the end of one); when nothing it names is reported there, or it names an…
printed:
warning[U07]: `wf-allow(U01)` allows nothing: no `U01` is reported on the line it covers
 --> src/App.wf:2:5
  |
2 |     // wf-allow(U01)
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Remove it — what it was written for is gone
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/U07
why:
A `// wf-allow(CODE)` comment accepts one finding on purpose: on a line of
its own it covers the next line of code, and at the end of a line it covers
that line. It names codes (`U01`) or families (`U`), comma-separated, and
only what `lints` could lower — a warning, or an error that ships no broken
page. An allow that covers nothing it names is reported, so allows cannot
outlive what they were written for.
fix: Remove the allow — what it was written for is gone.

title: Markup put in as markup
plain: Markup put in as markup
summary: An `Unsafe.Html`, and whether what it puts in went through `sanitize`; and a `Frame(srcdoc:)` drawing HTML from a value, which is sandboxed (`sandbox=""`) unless it says what it may do.
description: An `Unsafe.Html`, and whether what it puts in went through `sanitize`; and a `Frame(srcdoc:)` drawing HTML from a value, which is sandboxed…
printed:
warning[V03]: `Unsafe.Html` puts markup in as markup
 --> src/App.wf:4:5
  |
4 |     Unsafe.Html(body)
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Anything the project did not write itself belongs in `sanitize(…)` first
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/V03
fix:
Most text wants no markup of its own: write it as Markdown, which `Markdown(body)` draws with any HTML in it shown as text. Markup that must stay markup and comes from outside the project goes through `sanitize(…)` first — `Unsafe.Html(sanitize(body))` — which is the reviewed case, and the warning still names it. A `Frame(srcdoc:)` drawing HTML from a value is named too: that HTML is a document of its own, scripts and all. Unless the call says what the frame may do, it may do nothing — the build gives it `sandbox=""` — and the warning says so. Writing `sandbox:` out is the reviewed case; `allow-scripts` with `allow-same-origin` undoes the sandbox, and is named again. ```wf expect=V03 page P(path: "/", title: "T", description: "D") { state html = "

Hi

" Heading("Preview").h1 Frame(srcdoc: html, title: "Preview") } ``` ```text warning[V03]: `Frame(srcdoc:)` draws HTML from a value as a document; it is sandboxed (`sandbox=""`), so nothing in it runs --> src/App.wf:4:5 | 4 | Frame(srcdoc: html, title: "Preview") | ^^^^^ = help: Say what it may do with `sandbox:` — `sandbox: ""` keeps it as it is now; `allow-scripts` and `allow-same-origin` together undo the sandbox = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/V03 ``` **Fix:** `Frame(srcdoc: html, title: "Preview", sandbox: "")`.

title: A long list that is not windowed
plain: A long list that is not windowed
summary: A `VirtualList` draws only the rows in view of one keyed `for` — `for row in rows by row.id { … }` — that is the whole of its body; with anything else in it, or a `for` with no `by`, it draws everything, as a plain scrolling box does.
description: A `VirtualList` draws only the rows in view of one keyed `for` — `for row in rows by row.id { … }` — that is the whole of its body; with anything…
printed:
warning[V12]: This `VirtualList` draws every row: its body is not one keyed `for`
 --> src/App.wf:4:5
  |
4 |     VirtualList(rowHeight: 32) {
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^
  = help: Make its body one `for` with a `by`: `VirtualList(rowHeight: 32) { for row in rows by row.id { … } }`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/V12
why:
A `VirtualList` draws only the rows in view of the one keyed `for` that is
the whole of its body. With anything else beside the `for`, or a `for` with
no `by` — which has no way to keep a row's nodes as it scrolls — it draws
every row, as a plain scrolling box does, and the length of the list is
what the page pays for.
fix:
Give the `for` a `by`, and move anything else — a heading, a
count — outside the `VirtualList`.

title: A `Host` tag it does not make
plain: A Host tag it does not make
summary: A `Host` is made of one of a few elements — `div`, `span`, `canvas`, `svg`, `section`, `figure`, `pre`, `p`, `ul`, `table`; any other tag is a `div`.
description: A `Host` is made of one of a few elements — `div`, `span`, `canvas`, `svg`, `section`, `figure`, `pre`, `p`, `ul`, `table`; any other tag is a `div`.
printed:
warning[V10]: `Host` makes no `video`, so it is a `div`
 --> src/App.wf:3:10

3 |     Host(tag: "video", mount: (n) => n)
  |          ^^^
  = help: It makes `div`, `span`, `canvas`, `svg`, `section`, `figure`, `pre`, `p`, `ul`, `table`
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/V10
why:
A `Host` is made of one of a few elements: `div`, `span`, `canvas`, `svg`,
`section`, `figure`, `pre`, `p`, `ul` or `table` — the tag is written into
the document, so it is an allow-list rather than whatever the string says.
Any other tag is a `div`.
fix:
Make it one of the tags `Host` makes, or use the element the
built-ins offer for it (`Video`, `Audio`, `Image`).

title: A component named like a built-in
plain: A component named like a built-in
summary: A component the project declares takes the place of a built-in of its name: every call of the name draws the project's own, so the built-in cannot be placed in that project. A new built-in never changes what an existing project draws.
description: A component the project declares takes the place of a built-in of its name, so the built-in cannot be placed in that project.
printed:
info[V11]: `Chart` is this project's component, so a call of that name draws it rather than the built-in `Chart`
 --> src/App.wf:1:1
  |
1 | component Chart(_ title: String) {
  | ^^^^^^^^^
  = help: To place the built-in too, rename this one — `MyChart`, `ReportChart` — and its call sites
  = docs: https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/errors/V11
why:
A component the project declares takes the place of a built-in of the same
name: every call of the name draws the project's own component. This is
information (`info`), not a warning. Nothing is wrong, and a new built-in in a later
WebFluent never changes what an existing project draws. The one thing to
know is that the built-in of that name cannot be placed in this project.

To use the built-in as well, rename the component and its call sites:
fix:
Nothing needs fixing. To place the built-in too, rename the
component and its call sites; to stop the note, set `"lints": { "V11": "off" }`.
